chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade Al-Muhaqala and Al-Muzabana. I said, 'And what is it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Buying the fruit of the palm tree with the dates, and the crop with the wheat.'

key_terms.التَّمْرِ: Dates, typically referring to ripe or processed dates.
key_terms.الْمُحَاقَلَةِ: A type of sale where unripe grain is sold for ripe grain of the same kind.
key_terms.الْمُزَابَنَةِ: A type of sale where unripe fruit is sold for ripe fruit of the same kind.
key_terms.حَمْلُ النَّخْلِ: The fruit of the palm tree while still on the tree.

ai.seo_question: What are Al-Muhaqala and Al-Muzabana in Islamic trade law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the prohibition of Al-Muhaqala and Al-Muzabana, specific forms of deferred exchange sales involving agricultural produce, which the Imam defines as trading unripe fruit or grain for its processed counterpart. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on eliminating gharar (uncertainty) and riba (usury) in trade by ensuring the subject matter is clearly defined and possessed, a principle deeply rooted in the Prophet's practice as transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt.
